## Description

**What**: Update `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` to document the new `review.schema_correction_max_attempts` config key introduced by S-C.

**Why**: Reference docs are the canonical source operators consult before tuning a knob. Without this entry, the new key is invisible to anyone reading the reference doc, which is the doc-router Gate 2 trigger.

**Scope**:
- IN: One entry in `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` under the `review.*` namespace describing default, range, ceiling, clamping behavior, rationale for ceiling, and disambiguation from `review.max_resolution_attempts`.
- OUT: changes to `dso-config.conf` (S-C); any code changes (S-C).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` contains a new entry for `review.schema_correction_max_attempts` in the `review.*` namespace section with: default (1), documented intended range (0–3), hard ceiling (3), clamping behavior with warning log, rationale for ceiling (LLM cost containment), and explicit disambiguation from `review.max_resolution_attempts`
  ← Satisfies: doc-router Gate 2 (extends an existing reference doc)
- When this story is complete, the documentation includes a `DOC_ROUTER_ATTESTATION` block per `doc-router.md`

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] The existing entry for `review.max_resolution_attempts` is the direct precedent — match its formatting (default, allowed values, behavior, examples).
- Apply `/Users/joeoakhart/.claude/plugins/cache/digital-service-orchestra/dso-dev/1.17.0/skills/shared/prompts/doc-router.md` gates before writing. CLAUDE.md edits require a `CLAUDE_MD_SUGGESTED_CHANGE` report — do not edit CLAUDE.md directly. If `.claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md` exists, follow it for formatting.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
